CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Chorionic villi
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Pregnant patient referred for prenatal diagnosis following increased risk on non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) for trisomy 21.

PREVIOUS TESTING
- NIPT performed at [redacted location]: High risk for trisomy 21
- Rapid PCR on uncultured chorionic villi: Positive for trisomy 21

TEST PERFORMED
Targeted G-banded chromosome analysis focusing on chromosome 21
Rapid PCR analysis of uncultured chorionic villi for chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y

METHODOLOGY
Chorionic villi were cultured according to standard protocols. Metaphase chromosomes were obtained from cultured cells and G-banded using trypsin-Giemsa staining. A minimum of 20 metaphases were analyzed with particular attention to chromosome 21. Rapid PCR was performed on uncultured villi using quantitative fluorescent PCR (QF-PCR) with STR markers specific for chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y.

RESULTS

KARYOTYPE: 47,XX,+21

Targeted G-banded analysis detected three copies of chromosome 21 in all cells examined. The sex chromosome complement is female (XX). No other chromosomal abnormalities were detected in the regions analyzed.

RAPID PCR RESULTS:
- Chromosome 13: Two alleles detected (normal)
- Chromosome 18: Two alleles detected (normal)
- Chromosome 21: Three alleles detected (trisomy)
- Sex chromosomes: XX (female)

INTERPRETATION
The karyotype analysis reveals primary trisomy 21 with a female sex chromosome complement, consistent with Down syndrome. This finding confirms the previous NIPT screening result and rapid PCR analysis.

Primary trisomy 21 typically results from a spontaneous meiotic nondisjunction event during gametogenesis or less commonly from a post-zygotic mitotic error. The risk of trisomy 21 increases with maternal age.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
This finding confirms a diagnosis of Down syndrome in the fetus. Individuals with Down syndrome have intellectual disability of varying degrees, characteristic facial features, and increased risk for congenital heart defects, gastrointestinal anomalies, and other medical conditions. The presence of trisomy 21 in this pregnancy is associated with an increased risk for aneuploidy in future pregnancies, although the absolute risk remains relatively low.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss the implications of this diagnosis
2. Parental karyotyping is not indicated as primary trisomy 21 is typically a de novo event
3. For future pregnancies:
   - First and second trimester biochemical screening
   - Detailed ultrasound monitoring
   - Prenatal diagnosis (CVS or amniocentesis) is available if desired
4. Referral to pediatric specialists for postnatal care planning if pregnancy continues

This report has been reviewed and approved by:
[redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Director, Cytogenetics Laboratory
Board Certified Clinical Cytogeneticist
